A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoRAG study and contain 18 complete, readable pages, including Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of all dimensions.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoRAG evaluations on multi-hop QA and KILT, alongside scaling experiments, ablations and case analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, scaling experiments, ablations and appendix analyses unchanged.

M1.justification: The retrieval-chain generation procedure, training losses, decoding strategies and learned-stopping variant are identical in Sections 3 and 5.4. Appendix C's prompts also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four multi-hop QA datasets, KILT tasks, BLINK training data and Wikipedia retrieval corpus. No training or evaluation coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 1–3, including Self-RAG-7B, ITER-RETGEN, Search-o1-32B, the KILT baselines and the E5-base/BM25 controls.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain identical training budgets, sample counts, model configurations, decoding settings, metrics and validation-versus-test procedures.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same iterative-training, weak-to-strong, retriever robustness, early-stopping, sampling-budget and temperature analyses, together with the same HotpotQA cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting and run information are unchanged. The qualitative warning about Bamboogle's small sample and variability across runs remains identical in Section 4.2.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples match, including appendix results. For example, Table 1's CoRAG L=6 greedy 2WikiQA EM remains 70.6, and Table 2's CoRAG KILT NQ score remains 63.1.

T1.justification: Retrieval-chain definitions, likelihood scoring, training-loss formulas and mathematical descriptions of scaling are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about iterative retrieval, test-time scaling, multi-hop QA improvements and KILT performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including task-dependent scaling benefits, fine-tuning versus few-shot comparisons, Bamboogle's knowledge freshness, token-cost simplifications and early-stopping tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability sentence and a direct CoRAG repository link at the end of Section 1. v1 lacks this specific access pointer; implementation details and hyperparameters otherwise match.

R1.justification: Section 2, all 40 references and the positioning relative to earlier retrieval and reasoning methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: A single code-availability sentence is appended to the introduction, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added link reflows the final introduction paragraph and slightly changes heading spacing on page 2. Figures, tables and appendix layouts remain identical; rendered pages 3–18 match exactly.

improvement.justification: The direct implementation link added in Section 1 modestly improves resource discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but do not verify the linked code's completeness or functionality.
